blueprint_refs: Blueprint: "SBI calibration via NPE ... train NPE to approximate p(theta|x); sample posterior conditioned on x_o and take posterior mean as optimized_parameters"
CODING PATCH: "Use NPE on collected (theta, x) to learn p(theta | x)"

evidence.metrics: val_loss=259.1369 vs train_loss=135.8805; best_candidate loss on x_o is low (~6.94) but does not translate to dataset MSE.

calibration-does-not-follow-blueprint-np.error_identification: Posterior inference is effectively a regression-from-x-to-theta objective, and posterior sampling uses an artificial variance floor; the learned posterior mean (beta≈0.716, gamma≈0.104) yields poor generalization (validation MSE much worse than training).
calibration-does-not-follow-blueprint-np.root_cause_analysis: The implemented "NPE" is not NPE: _MLPGaussianNPE is trained to predict theta (in z-space) from x (supervised regression NLL), not to learn a conditional density consistent with a simulation-based likelihood-free posterior estimator. Additionally, SBINPECalibrator.fit forces std_o >= 0.15, injecting excessive posterior uncertainty unrelated to the learned model and potentially biasing posterior mean after sigmoid/logit transforms.
calibration-does-not-follow-blueprint-np.correct_approach: In SBINPECalibrator.fit, remove the hard posterior std floor and instead calibrate posterior spread from the network output (or a small, learned global std scaling). More importantly, restructure the estimator to be a proper conditional density model trained by maximizing log p_z(z|x) with a flexible conditional distribution (e.g., mixture density network with K Gaussians in z-space) rather than a single diagonal Gaussian that behaves like point-regression. Keep the prior bounds via z-transform. This is a structural change in _MLPGaussianNPE (output mixture weights/means/log_stds) and sampling (sample mixture component then z).
calibration-does-not-follow-blueprint-np.key_insight: If posterior samples/mean are sensitive to an arbitrary variance floor or a near-deterministic regressor, it is not doing SBI; use a conditional density family with enough capacity (e.g., mixture) and avoid hand-forced posterior uncertainty.

blueprint_refs: Blueprint: "sample posterior ... take posterior mean ... evaluate ... optionally run K stochastic rollouts"

evidence.metrics: val_loss remains high; posterior_predictive_num_thetas=50 and rollout deterministically uses posterior_samples[:50].

posterior-predictive-evaluation-uses-fir.error_identification: Posterior-predictive mean can be biased because evaluation uses the first 50 posterior draws rather than an unbiased subset/shuffle; this can over/under-represent parts of the posterior and increase MSE.
posterior-predictive-evaluation-uses-fir.root_cause_analysis: SBINPECalibrator.fit sets params._posterior_thetas = posterior_samples[:m_eval] without shuffling. DiscreteTimeSIRSimulator.rollout then uses posterior_thetas[:num_thetas_used] deterministically, so any ordering artifacts from sampling (or correlations) persist into predictions.
posterior-predictive-evaluation-uses-fir.correct_approach: In SBINPECalibrator.fit, randomly permute posterior_samples before selecting the m_eval subset (using the calibrator RNG). Alternatively, in DiscreteTimeSIRSimulator.rollout, draw theta indices at random per rollout (with replacement) from posterior_thetas to approximate posterior predictive expectation without dependence on ordering.
posterior-predictive-evaluation-uses-fir.key_insight: When approximating posterior predictive means with a finite theta set, always randomize or resample theta usage; never take a fixed prefix of samples.

blueprint_refs: Blueprint: "infer parameters from a single observed trajectory (train trajectory_id=0 only), then evaluate ... on full train/val/test sets."

evidence.metrics: train_loss=135.8805 but val_loss=259.1369 (large generalization gap). Per-dim: val_loss_per_dim.S=412.52 dominates.

objective-mismatch-single-trajectory-cal.error_identification: Even with seemingly reasonable inferred parameters, validation error is much larger than training error, especially in S; suggests the single observed trajectory is not representative of other trajectories under the assumed constant-parameter SIR.
objective-mismatch-single-trajectory-cal.root_cause_analysis: This may be an inherent identifiability/domain-shift limit: one trajectory (id 0) may not pin down a (beta,gamma) that explains heterogeneous trajectories. The current code also calibrates on raw counts MSE on the flattened vector; that objective overweights early high-S periods and trajectories with larger N, which can worsen cross-trajectory fit when N differs.
objective-mismatch-single-trajectory-cal.correct_approach: Within the blueprint constraint (use only trajectory_id=0 as observation for SBI), improve robustness by changing x representation during calibration: normalize x by N (use S/N, I/N, R/N) and/or use a variance-stabilized transform (e.g., sqrt counts) before feeding to NPE and computing best_candidate loss. Apply the same transform consistently to simulated x and x_o. This is a structural change in SBINPECalibrator.fit where x_o/x_sims are constructed. Be realistic: if trajectories truly require varying beta/gamma across ids, a single global theta cannot reach near-zero val_loss; the best achievable is likely bounded away from 1e-6.
objective-mismatch-single-trajectory-cal.key_insight: If calibrating from one trajectory but evaluating many, make the calibration observation vector scale-invariant (normalize by N / stabilize variance) to reduce mismatch across trajectories.
